title: Lecture 11. Socio-statistical research
summary:
1 Nature of Statistical Information

2 Key Indicators

1. Nature of Statistical Information There are various types of statistical information, built on different principles. State statistics are structured by territorial principle, while departmental statistics are structured by industry. However, these are not entirely different statistics. State statistical information includes key or most aggregated types of industry-specific information, but calculated by territory. Although some industry-specific information is also compiled by territory.

Any statistical system is primarily designed to reflect two unrelated processes:

a) the facts or phenomena themselves in a given territory (morbidity, crime, etc.) b) the activities of certain departments or services that deal with these facts (healthcare, police, etc.). The problem is that statistics are maintained by relevant state bodies, and almost all statistical information describes the activities of these bodies themselves, rather than the phenomena. Suppose we are interested in statistics on offenses committed while intoxicated. Such records are kept worldwide. Upon receiving the relevant data, we learn how many people were detained. Morbidity statistics are essentially statistics on visits to medical institutions. Consequently, this is the biggest source of errors in state statistics. In fact, it reflects the activities of a bureaucratic organization interested in presenting facts favorably for itself.

Sources of statistical data distortion:

Intentional underreporting of data to conceal the scale of a phenomenon; Overstating data that favorably characterizes the activities of a department; Intentional distortion of data due to the complexity of their interpretation; Abbreviated publication of data: not in absolute figures, but in percentages or fractions, or per thousand population, without absolute figures for baseline calculation; Non-systematic errors or errors in accounting and compilation due to shortcomings or complexity of the compilation procedure itself (human factor); Latency of recorded phenomena (socially disapproved behaviors most often "escape" observation).

2. Key Indicators Morbidity (prevalence)

Number of drug addiction patients registered in narcological institutions of the Russian Federation at the end of the reporting year, according to the Federal State Statistics Service, thousand people.

Incidence (new cases)

Patients with a first-time diagnosis of drug addiction taken under dispensary observation in narcological institutions of the Russian Federation at the end of the reporting year, according to the Federal State Statistics Service, thousand people.

Tasks: Compare the PREVALENCE of HIV infection in the population of 2 regions

Region 1 (population 51,000 people), number of HIV-infected individuals – 100, number of individuals with a first-time diagnosis of HIV infection in 2012 – 10.

Region 2 (population 155,000 people), number of HIV-infected individuals – 120, number of individuals with a first-time diagnosis of HIV infection in 2012 – 70.

Region 1:

100 / 51,000 x 1000 = 1.96

Region 2:

120 / 155,000 x 1000 = 0.77

Compare the INCIDENCE of HIV infection among the population of 2 regions:

Region 1 (population 7,200,000 people), number of HIV-infected individuals – 33,000, number of individuals with a first-time diagnosis of HIV infection in 2012 – 1000.

Region 2 (population 2,400,000 people), number of HIV-infected individuals – 33,000, number of individuals with a first-time diagnosis of HIV infection in 2012 – 700.

Region 1:

1000 / 7,200,000 x 100,000 = 13.89

Region 2:

700 / 2,400,000 x 100,000 = 29.17
